name: 40 Hz gamma, magnetic sine (GENUS timing)
origin: Rhythm from the Tsai lab's GENUS light and sound flicker (MIT Picower Institute; Cognito Therapeutics trials); the magnetic version is a project construct
summary: A 40 Hz sine field (50 points per cycle) on all eight ring coils in phase for 1 h, the smooth alternative to the square version of this GENUS-inspired program. GENUS is light and sound flicker; a magnetic 40 Hz field is not GENUS and has no evidence.
notes: GENUS (gamma entrainment using sensory stimuli) is an LED flickering 12.5 ms on / 12.5 ms off at 40 Hz (Iaccarino 2016) and, in Martorell 2019, also a 1-ms 10 kHz tone every 25 ms aligned to the light onset, 1 h a day. The research protocol offers a 40 Hz sine with 50 points per cycle (0.5 ms each) as an alternative to the on/off square (lowfield-gamma-40hz-square); both run on the full ring with all coils in phase. The optional LED and audio channel needs new hardware (a GPIO-driven LED and I2S audio on the ESP32) and is left out, so the part of GENUS that has data is missing here. The sensory results are themselves contested: Soula 2023 found no gamma entrainment or amyloid change from 40 Hz light in mice, the human data are small trials (e.g. Chan 2022), and a meta-analysis (Ang 2025) found no established cognitive benefit. This program is not a treatment for Alzheimer's disease or any other condition. The research sets 5 uT, the top of the app's range; the app caps it at the coils' calibrated maximum (about 3-6 uT at 20 mm). If you add 40 Hz light flicker from another device, screen for photosensitive epilepsy first and offer a sound-only mode; the same meta-analysis raised a tinnitus signal for the sound. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Seated and relaxed, eyes open or closed, in a quiet room.
schedule: The GENUS studies used 1 h a day (Chan et al. 2022: daily for 3 months). No schedule has been tested for a magnetic 40 Hz field.
source: Iaccarino et al. 2016, Nature 540:230 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5656389/ ; Martorell et al. 2019, Cell 177:256 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774262/ ; Soula et al. 2023, Nat Neurosci https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10839995/ ; Chan et al. 2022, PLoS One https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9714926/ ; Ang et al. 2025, meta-analysis https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12700959/
